# v2.98-dev

A change to how quickly a permission change takes effect.

## Fixed

- **Changing someone's role now applies immediately, instead of whenever they
  next sign in.** Until now, a person's role travelled with their signed-in
  session. If you changed it while they were logged in, the old role stayed in
  force for as long as that session lasted — up to eight hours — so someone you
  had just moved out of an administrator role could keep using administrator
  pages for the rest of the working day. The Users page showed the new role the
  whole time, which made it look as though the change had taken.

  Changing a role now ends that person's open sessions. They sign back in and
  continue with their new role, and the change applies from their very next
  action. The same applies to company access, which for a system-wide
  administrator was following the stale role rather than the saved setting.

- **"Require MFA at next login" now takes effect on the current session too.**
  Ticking it for someone already signed in previously did nothing until they
  happened to log out, which could be days. They are now asked to set up
  two-factor authentication straight away.

- **Editing only a display name does not sign anyone out**, and **changing your
  own role keeps you signed in** — you carry on immediately with the new role
  rather than being logged out by your own edit. Your session's overall time
  limit is not extended by this.

- Editing a user who no longer exists now reports that plainly instead of
  failing with a server error.

## Upgrading

No action needed. The one visible change is that people whose role you change
will be asked to sign in again.
